_comment: The third registered collective with no workload file anywhere in the repo.
It is not another all_reduce. vendor_impl_run issues dist.all_reduce(async_op=True)
and then a host-to-device copy while that all_reduce is in flight, so what it
measures is *overlap*: whether the collective and the host DMA proceed at once, or
serialise. That is the single most load-bearing overlap in TP inference -- the
attention/MLP all_reduce against the next H2D -- and neither backend has a number
for it. Compare each row against all_reduce.json and host2device.json at the same
size: if latency is close to max(the two), the two engines overlap; if it is close
to their sum, they do not.
Two quirks of the op def to read the numbers with, neither of them fixable from a
workload file:
* the all_reduce is issued on the *default* group, not op_group, so it always
spans every rank the launch started, while world_size here only feeds the
bus_size formula. So launch with exactly as many devices as world_size asks
for, or bus_bw is computed for a group that was not the one used.
* async_op=True is never waited on -- there is no req.wait() -- so the measured
latency bounds the H2D plus whatever of the all_reduce the timing barrier
happens to catch, and a suspiciously low number means the collective escaped
the window rather than that the overlap is perfect.
int8 is absent because the op def gates dtype to the three float formats.
world_size is capped at 8 and batch_size at 262144: this op holds four buffers of
the payload (device data + its output, host src, device dst), so it hits the 24 GiB
per logical core ceiling twice as early as a plain all_reduce.
